_about: Table IA.VIII, Signal Definitions and Citations. One row per column of the 145-column Stage-2 panel: 108 sorted signals plus 37 identifiers, returns and characteristics. Extracted from the paper's longtable, then reconciled against Stage 2's DATA_DICTIONARY.md and the code that computes each signal. A row carrying `paper_prints` or `paper_prints_citation` is one where the two disagreed and the code settled it; `why_corrected` says what settled it. Everything else is the paper's text unchanged. See RECONCILIATION_ia08.md.

rows.name: Bond Identifier
rows.description: 9-digit CUSIP bond identifier.

rows.name: Date
rows.description: True month-end date (YYYY-MM-DD).

rows.name: Issuer CUSIP
rows.description: 6-digit firm identifier (first 6 digits of CUSIP).

rows.name: CRSP PERMNO
rows.description: CRSP permanent security identifier.

rows.name: CRSP PERMCO
rows.description: CRSP permanent company identifier.

rows.name: Compustat GVKEY
rows.description: Compustat global company key.

rows.name: Holding Period
rows.description: NYSE trading sessions from the start trade (dt_s) to the end trade (dt_e) of the month-end return (see Fig. \ref{fig:return_timeline}). Runs 15 to 27, because each trade may fall anywhere in the last 5 sessions of its month.
rows.paper_prints: Month-end holding period in calendar days (see Fig. \ref{fig:return_timeline}).
rows.why_corrected: The printed row says calendar days. It was never calendar days. Until 2026-09-21 stage2/steps/step1_returns.py counted NYSE sessions from dt_s to the CALENDAR month-end, a date the return does not use; it now counts to dt_e, the end trade, so the column is the window of the return printed beside it. contract.assert_holding_period_is_the_window checks it on every row of every build.

rows.name: Latent Implementation Bias
rows.description: Clean price return from month-end to the next month-begin. On the row for month $t$: $\text{LIB}_t = P_{t+1}^{\text{bgn}} / P_t^{\text{end}} - 1$, the gap that FOLLOWS that month's end price (see Fig. \ref{fig:return_timeline}).
rows.paper_prints: Clean price return from month-end to month-begin: $\text{LIB} = P_t^{\text{bgn}} / P_{t-1}^{\text{end}} - 1$ (see Fig. \ref{fig:return_timeline}).
rows.why_corrected: The printed row writes $P_t^{bgn} / P_{t-1}^{end} - 1$, stamping the gap with the month its begin price falls in. The panel stamps it with the month-end price it follows: step1_returns.py re-dates the gap to t-1 before merging it onto the end frame. Recomputed from the daily prices on all 1,650,561 rows that carry lib, the forward form matches every row and the printed form matches 2,192. Same object, and the row it sits on is what a user joining on date needs to know.

rows.name: LIB (Dirty)
rows.description: LIB computed using dirty prices (includes accrued interest and coupon).

rows.name: Return Type
rows.description: Return classification: standard, trad_in_def, or default_evnt.

rows.name: FF17 Industry
rows.description: Fama-French 17-industry classification.

rows.name: FF30 Industry
rows.description: Fama-French 30-industry classification.

rows.name: Market Cap (Start)
rows.description: Bond market capitalization at end of month $t{-}1$.

rows.name: Market Cap (End)
rows.description: Bond market capitalization at end of month $t$.

rows.name: Treasury Return
rows.description: Duration-matched U.S. Treasury portfolio return: the CRSP fixed-term Treasury returns interpolated at the bond's modified duration, rounded to 2 decimals, on its month-end trade date ($dt_e$). That is the unadjusted duration, not the panel's gap-adjusted \texttt{md\_dur}. Used to compute duration-adjusted returns: $r^x = r - tret$.
rows.paper_prints: Duration-matched U.S. Treasury portfolio return. Used to compute duration-adjusted returns: $r^x = r - tret$.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row leaves the duration unstated, and the dictionary said `md_dur`. `_attach_tret` in `stage2/steps/step1_returns.py` reads `mod_dur` on the month-end trade row, where the return ends; the panel's `md_dur` is read at the signal date, before it.

rows.name: Treasury Return, Duration-Weighted Cash Flows
rows.description: Treasury benchmark built from the bond's own cash flows, weighted by their present-value shares (Macaulay duration weights) and applied to zero-coupon Treasury returns from the Gurkaynak-Sack-Wright curve. Subtract from \texttt{ret\_vw} for a duration-adjusted return.

rows.name: Treasury Return, Cash-Flow-Weighted
rows.description: As \texttt{tret\_bns}, but weighting the same cash flows by their future value rather than their present value. Places more weight on long-dated cash flows and so overstates a bond's interest rate risk; reported as the authors' own robustness alternative.
rows.citation: van Binsbergen, Nozawa, and Schwert (2025), Internet Appendix A1
rows.citation_text: van Binsbergen, Nozawa, and Schwert (2025), Internet Appendix A1

rows.name: Treasury Return, Exact Duration Match
rows.description: As \texttt{tret\_bns}, refined so the Treasury portfolio's duration equals the bond's exactly. The present-value weights are duration-matched only when the term structure is flat; this solves for the Treasury yield that restores the match and reweights accordingly.
rows.citation: Ghaderi, Plante, Roussanov, and Seo (2026), Appendix B.2
rows.citation_text: Ghaderi, Plante, Roussanov, and Seo (2026), Appendix B.2

rows.name: Treasury Return, Cash-Flow-Matched
rows.description: As \texttt{tret\_bns}, but discounting the same cash flows on the Treasury zero curve instead of at the bond's own yield to maturity. This replicates the bond's cash flows rather than its duration, so it removes slope and curvature effects as well as parallel shifts. The difference from \texttt{tret\_bns} is the authors' higher-order component.

rows.name: Treasury Return, Maturity-Matched
rows.description: The twin of \texttt{tret}: the same key-rate Treasury index returns, the same interpolation nodes and rounding, but interpolated at the bond's remaining MATURITY rather than its modified duration. Included as the maturity-matched comparator; duration matching is the more precise of the two.

rows.name: Total Return (End)
rows.description: Month-end to month-end total return (see Fig. \ref{fig:return_timeline}).

rows.name: Total Return (Begin)
rows.description: Month-begin to month-end total return within the same month (see Fig. \ref{fig:return_timeline}).

rows.name: Date Start
rows.description: Trade date for month-end price in month $t{-}1$ (last 5 BD); refer to Panel A of Fig. \ref{fig:return_timeline}.

rows.name: Date End
rows.description: Trade date for month-end price in month $t$ (last 5 BD); refer to Panel A of Fig. \ref{fig:return_timeline}.

rows.name: Date Start (Begin)
rows.description: Trade date for month-begin price in month $t$ (first 5 BD); refer to Panel C of Fig. \ref{fig:return_timeline}.

rows.name: Date End (Begin)
rows.description: Trade date for month-end price in month $t$ (last 5 BD) for begin returns; refer to Panel C of Fig. \ref{fig:return_timeline}.

rows.name: Holding Period (Begin)
rows.description: NYSE trading sessions from the month-begin trade (dt_s_bgn) to the month-end trade (dt_e_bgn) of the same month.
rows.paper_prints: Month-begin holding period in calendar days.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row says calendar days. stage2/steps/step1_returns.py counts NYSE sessions between the two trades of the month-begin return (cal_lut cum_before at dt minus at date_start), and always has. Observed range 10 to 22.

rows.name: Implementation Gap
rows.description: NYSE trading sessions from the last session of month $t{-}1$ to the month-begin trade of month $t$ (dt_s_bgn); 1 to 5. Refer to Panel D of Fig. \ref{fig:return_timeline}.
rows.paper_prints: Business days between month-end price ($t{-}1$) and month-begin price ($t$); capped at 5 BD. Refer to Panel D of Fig. \ref{fig:return_timeline}.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row measures from the month-end PRICE of t-1. The code measures from the last NYSE SESSION of t-1 (date_end_bus_lag), whether or not the bond traded that day: that form matches all 1,801,790 rows, and measuring from the month-end trade matches 1,215,816 of 1,584,054.

rows.name: Signal Date
rows.description: Date when price-based signal was observed (minimum 1 BD before month-end price). Refer to Panel B of Fig. \ref{fig:return_timeline}.

rows.name: Signal Gap
rows.description: Business days between signal observation and month-end price; ranges 1--10 BD. Refer to Panel B of Fig. \ref{fig:return_timeline}.

rows.name: Risk-Free Rate
rows.description: Monthly risk-free rate from Fama-French. Used for excess returns, $r - r^f$.
rows.paper_prints: Monthly risk-free rate from Fama-French. Used for excess returns: $r^x = r - r^f$.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row writes the excess return as $r^x$, the symbol this table uses for the duration-adjusted return $r - tret$. The two are different returns, so the symbol is dropped here.

rows.name: S&P Composite Rating
rows.description: Composite credit rating: S&P rating if available, otherwise Moody's rating. Scale: 1 (AAA) to 21 (C), 22 = Default.
rows.paper_prints: Composite credit rating: S&P rating if available, otherwise Moody's rating. Scale: 1 (AAA) to 21 (CCC-), 22 = Default.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row labels rating 21 as CCC-. On the numeric scale Stage 1 builds (stage1/helper_functions.convert_sp_to_numeric), CCC- is 19, CC is 20, C is 21 and D is 22. The scale's range is right; only the label on its last non-default grade is wrong.

rows.name: Moody's Composite Rating
rows.description: Composite credit rating: Moody's rating if available, otherwise S&P rating. Scale: 1 (Aaa) to 21 (C), 22 = Default.
rows.paper_prints: Composite credit rating: Moody's rating if available, otherwise S&P rating. Scale: 1 (AAA) to 20 (CCC-), 21 = Default.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row says 1--20 with 21 = Default. Its own `spc_rat` row, one line above, says 1--21 with 22 = Default for the identical scale, and so does Stage 2's data dictionary. The paper contradicts itself; the 21/22 scale is the one the data uses. Rating 21 is C, not CCC- (CCC- and Caa3 are 19; see stage1/helper_functions.convert_sp_to_numeric and convert_moodys_to_numeric).

rows.name: Callable Indicator
rows.description: Indicator for embedded call option (1 = callable, 0 = non-callable).

rows.name: Face Value
rows.description: Bond amount outstanding (face value), in thousands of dollars.
rows.paper_prints: Bond amount outstanding (face value); units of the bond outstanding.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row says units of the bond outstanding. The column is FISD's amount outstanding, which FISD reports in thousands of dollars: its median on the 2026-09-21 panel is 500,000, a $500 million issue.

rows.name: Rule 144A Indicator
rows.description: Dummy variable: 1 if bond is Rule 144A, 0 otherwise.

rows.name: Country
rows.description: The issuer's country of domicile, from FISD \texttt{country\_domicile} (e.g., USA).
rows.paper_prints: Country of issuance (e.g., USA for U.S. bonds).
rows.why_corrected: The printed row says country of issuance. `stage2/steps/step7_final.py` reads FISD's `country_domicile`, which is where the issuer is domiciled.

rows.name: Time to Maturity
rows.description: Years remaining until bond maturity.

rows.name: Bond Age
rows.description: Years since bond issuance.

rows.name: Yield to Maturity
rows.description: Annualized yield to maturity. Computed with QuantLib.

rows.name: Credit Spread
rows.description: Annualized credit spread: yield minus maturity-matched U.S. Treasury yield.

rows.name: Modified Duration
rows.description: Modified duration measuring price sensitivity to yield changes. Computed with QuantLib.

rows.name: Convexity
rows.description: Second-order price sensitivity to yield changes. Computed with QuantLib.

rows.name: Bond Size
rows.description: Bond market capitalization: dirty price times amount outstanding (\$ millions).

rows.name: 6-Month Spread Narrowing (log)
rows.description: Log change in credit spread over prior 6 months: $\log(cs_{t-6}) - \log(cs_t)$. If the spread is missing exactly 6 months ago, the nearest adjacent month is used within a $\pm$1 month band, the EARLIER month first.
rows.paper_prints: Log change in credit spread over prior 6 months: $\log(cs_{t-6}) - \log(cs_t)$. If spread is missing exactly 6 months ago, the nearest adjacent spread is used within a $\pm$2 month band, with $+$ favored over $-$.
rows.why_corrected: Measured in the code, not inferred: `_stage2_settings.DSPREAD_BANDWIDTH = 1`, and `lib/value.py` builds `offsets = [0, -1, +1]`, so the search is one month either side and prefers the earlier month (the longer lag). The printed row says a $\pm$2 band with `+` favoured over `-` -- wrong in the width AND backwards in the tie-break. `dcs6` is an FDR survivor, so this is not cosmetic.

rows.name: 12-Month Average Spread
rows.description: Average credit spread over the bond's 12 monthly observations before month $t$, month $t{-}1$ included. Requires minimum 6 observations.
rows.paper_prints: Rolling 12-month average credit spread, skipping the prior month. Requires minimum 6 observations.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row says it skips the prior month. `stage2/lib/value.py` shifts the spread by one row and averages the 12 rows before it (at least 6), so month $t{-}1$ is in the window and month $t$ is the one left out. On the 2026-09-21 run the published column equals that average on 100% of 1,665,078 rows, and the version that skips $t{-}1$ on under 0.5%.

rows.name: Bond Book-to-Market
rows.description: Par price divided by market price of the bond. All bonds have a par value of \$1,000 (100%).

rows.name: Value (HZ)
rows.description: Percentage deviation of observed credit spread from fitted ``fair'' spread: $(cs - \widehat{cs}) / \widehat{cs}$. Controls: rating, industry, 3-month spread change, callable. Fitted spread is estimated each month via cross-sectional regression; because cs is used, this signal is also exposed to microstructure noise.
rows.paper_prints: Percentage deviation of observed credit spread from fitted ``fair'' spread: $(cs - \widehat{cs}) / \widehat{cs}$. Controls: rating, industry, maturity, spread change, callable. Fitted spread is estimated each month via cross-sectional regression; because cs is used, this signal is also exposed to microstructure noise.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row lists maturity among the controls. The regression has no maturity control: stage2/lib/value.py calls compute_value(model_type='hz', x_cols=['dcs3', 'call']) with rating and FF17 industry dummies, and nothing else enters.

rows.name: Value (HZ, DtS-adjusted)
rows.description: HZ value signal demeaned within duration-times-spread quintiles to control for systematic spread-duration risk.

rows.name: Value (IPR)
rows.description: Log-spread residual from fair-value regression: $\log(cs) - X'\hat{\beta}$. Controls: rating, industry, log duration, volatility, callable. Fitted spread is estimated each month via cross-sectional regression; because cs is used, this signal is also exposed to microstructure noise.

rows.name: Value (IPR, DtS-adjusted)
rows.description: IPR value signal demeaned within duration-times-spread quintiles.

rows.name: 3-Month Momentum
rows.description: Cumulative return months $t{-}2$ to $t{-}1$, skipping month $t$.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row cites `gebhardt2005cross` -- Gebhardt, Hvidkjaer and Swaminathan (2005), *The cross-section of expected corporate bond returns: betas or characteristics?*. Bond momentum is the OTHER GHS 2005 paper, *Stock and bond market interaction: does momentum spill over?*, `gebhardt2005stock`. Same authors, same year, same journal, different result. The printed description says it skips the prior month; the month it skips is t, the row's own month, which is what `str` holds.
rows.paper_prints: Cumulative return months $t{-}2$ to $t{-}1$, skipping prior month.

rows.name: 6-Month Momentum
rows.description: Cumulative return months $t{-}5$ to $t{-}1$.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row cites `gebhardt2005cross` -- Gebhardt, Hvidkjaer and Swaminathan (2005), *The cross-section of expected corporate bond returns: betas or characteristics?*. Bond momentum is the OTHER GHS 2005 paper, *Stock and bond market interaction: does momentum spill over?*, `gebhardt2005stock`. Same authors, same year, same journal, different result.

rows.name: 12-Month Momentum
rows.description: Cumulative return months $t{-}11$ to $t{-}1$.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row cites `gebhardt2005cross` -- Gebhardt, Hvidkjaer and Swaminathan (2005), *The cross-section of expected corporate bond returns: betas or characteristics?*. Bond momentum is the OTHER GHS 2005 paper, *Stock and bond market interaction: does momentum spill over?*, `gebhardt2005stock`. Same authors, same year, same journal, different result.

rows.name: Intermediate Momentum
rows.description: Cumulative return months $t{-}11$ to $t{-}7$, excluding recent returns.

rows.name: Systematic Momentum (6-1)
rows.description: Sum of fitted values over months $t{-}5$ to $t{-}1$ from a 36(12) rolling CAPMB regression (bond market factor).

rows.name: Idiosyncratic Momentum (6-1)
rows.description: Sum of residuals over months $t{-}5$ to $t{-}1$ from a 36(12) rolling CAPMB regression (bond market factor).

rows.name: Industry Momentum (12-1)
rows.description: The equal-weighted return of all bonds sharing its SIC code (FISD), the bond itself included, compounded over months $t{-}11$ to $t{-}1$.
rows.paper_prints: Equal-weighted average 12-1 momentum of other bonds in the same FF17 industry.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row says the average signal of OTHER bonds in the same FF17 industry. stage2/lib/momentum.py averages the returns of every bond sharing the FISD sic_code in a month, the bond itself included, and compounds that industry return over the window; there is no FF17 grouping and no exclusion. Every (sic_code, month) group carries one value.

rows.name: Long-Term Reversal (48-12)
rows.description: Cumulative return months $t{-}47$ to $t{-}12$. Uses expanding window starting at 12-3, ramping to 48-12.

rows.name: Long-Term Reversal (30-6)
rows.description: Cumulative return months $t{-}29$ to $t{-}6$. Uses expanding window starting at 12-3, ramping to 30-6.

rows.name: Industry LTR (48-12)
rows.description: The equal-weighted return of all bonds sharing its SIC code (FISD), the bond itself included, compounded over months $t{-}47$ to $t{-}12$. Uses expanding window starting at 12-3, ramping to 48-12.
rows.paper_prints: Equal-weighted average 48-12 LTR of other bonds in the same FF17 industry.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row says the average signal of OTHER bonds in the same FF17 industry. stage2/lib/momentum.py averages the returns of every bond sharing the FISD sic_code in a month, the bond itself included, and compounds that industry return over the window; there is no FF17 grouping and no exclusion. Every (sic_code, month) group carries one value.

rows.name: Short-Term Reversal
rows.description: The return over month $t$, the most recent month and the one the momentum signals skip, measured with the signal gap. The unadjusted twin \texttt{str\_mmn} is \texttt{ret\_vw} itself.
rows.paper_prints: Prior month return $r_{t-1}$.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row says the prior month, r_{t-1}. On the row for month t the column holds the return over month t itself, measured with the signal gap: on the 2026 panel it correlates 0.90 with ret_vw on the same row and -0.04 with the row before. It is the month the momentum signals skip, since mom3_1 on the same row covers t-2 to t-1.

rows.name: 9-Month Momentum
rows.description: Cumulative return months $t{-}8$ to $t{-}1$.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row cites `gebhardt2005cross` -- Gebhardt, Hvidkjaer and Swaminathan (2005), *The cross-section of expected corporate bond returns: betas or characteristics?*. Bond momentum is the OTHER GHS 2005 paper, *Stock and bond market interaction: does momentum spill over?*, `gebhardt2005stock`. Same authors, same year, same journal, different result.

rows.name: Systematic Momentum (3-1)
rows.description: Sum of fitted values over months $t{-}2$ to $t{-}1$ from a 36(12) rolling CAPMB regression.

rows.name: Systematic Momentum (12-1)
rows.description: Sum of fitted values over months $t{-}11$ to $t{-}1$ from a 36(12) rolling CAPMB regression.

rows.name: Idiosyncratic Momentum (3-1)
rows.description: Sum of residuals over months $t{-}2$ to $t{-}1$ from a 36(12) rolling CAPMB regression.

rows.name: Idiosyncratic Momentum (12-1)
rows.description: Sum of residuals over months $t{-}11$ to $t{-}1$ from a 36(12) rolling CAPMB regression.

rows.name: Industry Momentum (1)
rows.description: The equal-weighted return in month $t{-}1$ of all bonds sharing its SIC code (FISD), the bond itself included.

rows.why_corrected: The printed row says the average signal of OTHER bonds in the same FF17 industry. stage2/lib/momentum.py averages the returns of every bond sharing the FISD sic_code in a month, the bond itself included, and compounds that industry return over the window; there is no FF17 grouping and no exclusion. Every (sic_code, month) group carries one value.

rows.description: The equal-weighted return of all bonds sharing its SIC code (FISD), the bond itself included, compounded over months $t{-}2$ to $t{-}1$.
rows.paper_prints: Equal-weighted average 3-1 momentum of other bonds in the same FF17 industry.

Every (sic_code, month) group carries one value.

rows.name: Long-Term Reversal (24-3)
rows.description: Cumulative return months $t{-}23$ to $t{-}3$. Uses expanding window starting at 12-3.

rows.name: Industry LTR (30-6)
rows.description: The equal-weighted return of all bonds sharing its SIC code (FISD), the bond itself included, compounded over months $t{-}29$ to $t{-}6$. Uses expanding window starting at 12-3, ramping to 30-6.
rows.paper_prints: Equal-weighted average 30-6 LTR of other bonds in the same FF17 industry.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row says the average signal of OTHER bonds in the same FF17 industry. stage2/lib/momentum.py averages the returns of every bond sharing the FISD sic_code in a month, the bond itself included, and compounds that industry return over the window; there is no FF17 grouping and no exclusion. Every (sic_code, month) group carries one value.

rows.description: The equal-weighted return of all bonds sharing its SIC code (FISD), the bond itself included, compounded over months $t{-}23$ to $t{-}3$. Uses expanding window starting at 12-3.
rows.paper_prints: Equal-weighted average 24-3 LTR of other bonds in the same FF17 industry.

rows.name: Price Impact
rows.description: Pastor-Stambaugh liquidity: negated coefficient from return reversal regression on signed volume. Requires a minimum of 5 daily returns.

rows.name: Amihud Illiquidity
rows.description: Within-month mean of daily $|r_t|/\text{dvol}_t$. Requires a minimum of 5 daily returns.

rows.name: Amihud Volatility
rows.description: Monthly standard deviation of daily Amihud ratios. Requires a minimum of 5 daily returns.

rows.name: Roll Spread
rows.description: Implicit bid-ask spread: $2\sqrt{\max(-\text{Cov}(r_t, r_{t-1}), 0)}$, with $r_t$ the daily log clean-price return in percent, so the spread is in percent of price. Requires a minimum of 5 daily returns.
rows.paper_prints: Implicit bid-ask spread: $2\sqrt{\max(-\text{Cov}(r_t, r_{t-1}), 0)}$. Requires a minimum of 5 daily returns.
rows.why_corrected: The printed formula leaves the units open. `stage2/lib/illiq_pandas.py` builds it from log returns multiplied by 100, the covariance behind `ilq`, so a value of 0.47 is 0.47% of price.

rows.name: Roll Autocovariance
rows.description: Negative autocovariance of the bond's daily log clean-price returns, the returns taken in percent (log return $\times 100$), so 10,000 times the autocovariance of decimal returns. Requires a minimum of 5 daily returns.
rows.paper_prints: Negative autocovariance of log returns $\times 100$. Requires a minimum of 5 daily returns.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row reads as the autocovariance multiplied by 100. `stage2/lib/illiq_pandas.py` multiplies each log return by 100 before taking the covariance, which scales the covariance by 10,000.

rows.name: Relative Bid-Ask Spread
rows.description: Dollar-volume-weighted average dealer ask minus average dealer bid, over their midpoint. No minimum: a month with one bid and one ask has a value.
rows.paper_prints: Volume-weighted $(P^{ask} - P^{bid})/\text{mid}$. Requires a minimum of 5 prices.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row requires a minimum of 5 prices. As for `spd_abs`, the code applies none.

rows.name: Corwin-Schultz Spread
rows.description: High-low spread estimator using two-day price ranges. Requires a minimum of 5 prices.

rows.name: Abdi-Ranaldo Spread
rows.description: Closing price spread estimator. Requires a minimum of 5 prices.

rows.name: No-Trade Day Proportion
rows.description: Fraction of the month's business days with no valid price. In the published (gap-adjusted) form the bond's last trading day in the month counts as a day without one, so the value is at least one over the month's business days; the unadjusted share is \texttt{p\_zro\_mmn}. Returns are never inspected, so the old name "Zero-Return Proportion" contradicted this description.
rows.paper_prints: Fraction of business days with no valid price.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row is the unadjusted share. `stage2/steps/step2_illiquidity.py` builds the adjusted share by leaving the last trading day out of the priced days, and the panel carries that form: on the 2026-09-21 panel it is never 0 (its minimum is 0.0435) and it exceeds `p_zro_mmn` on all 1,933,258 rows where both exist, while `p_zro_mmn` is 0 on 350,662. The printed name was "Zero-Return Proportion"; the column counts days without a price and never looks at returns.

rows.name: FHT Spread
rows.description: Spread derived from the no-trade proportion: $2\sigma\Phi^{-1}((1+p_{zro})/2)$, where $p_{zro}$ is always the full-month share, while in the published form $\sigma$ leaves out the bond's last day of trading. Requires a minimum of 5 daily returns.
rows.paper_prints: Spread derived from zero-return proportion: $2\sigma\Phi^{-1}((1+p_{zro})/2)$. Requires a minimum of 5 daily returns.
rows.why_corrected: The printed formula reads as if it used the panel's own `p_zro`. In the published (gap-adjusted) form, `stage2/steps/step2_illiquidity.py` combines the adjusted $\sigma$ with the FULL-month $p_{zro}$, while the panel's `p_zro` column is the adjusted share.

rows.name: Volatility-over-Volume
rows.description: Liquidity proxy: $2.5 \times \sigma^{0.6} / \bar{V}^{0.25}$, where $\sigma$ is the volatility of daily RETURNS and $\bar{V}$ mean volume. Requires a minimum of 5 daily returns. Not the volatility OF volume.

rows.name: Negative LIX (Illiquidity)
rows.description: $-\log_{10}[(V \times P_{\text{close}}) / (P_{\text{high}} - P_{\text{low}})]$, averaged over the month's days whose high differs from their low. Requires a minimum of 5 daily Amihud ratios (a daily return with positive volume), the count \texttt{ami} uses. Stored NEGATED (lib/illiq_pandas.py), so it rises with ILLIQUIDITY -- 99.29% of non-null values are negative, median -2.181.
rows.paper_prints: $\log_{10}[(V \times P_{\text{close}}) / (P_{\text{high}} - P_{\text{low}})]$. Requires a minimum of 5 prices.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row requires 5 prices. `stage2/lib/illiq_pandas.py` gates it on 5 daily Amihud ratios, the same count as `ami`, and a day whose high equals its low has no value, so it is left out of the mean. The printed row, named "LIX Liquidity", also had no minus sign: the column is stored negated, so it rises with illiquidity.

rows.name: Absolute Bid-Ask Spread
rows.description: Dollar-volume-weighted average dealer ask price minus average dealer bid price over the month, in points of par. No minimum: a month with one bid and one ask has a value.
rows.paper_prints: Volume-weighted $(P^{ask} - P^{bid})$ in dollars. Requires a minimum of 5 prices.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row requires a minimum of 5 prices. `stage2/steps/step2_illiquidity.py` applies none to the two Hong-Warga spreads: on the 2026-09-21 run 78,937 published values come from months with fewer than 5 priced days, the fewest 2.

rows.name: Daily Volatility
rows.description: Standard deviation of daily returns within the month.

rows.name: Daily Skewness
rows.description: Central skewness of daily returns within the month.

rows.name: Daily Kurtosis
rows.description: Excess kurtosis of daily returns within the month.

rows.name: Realized Volatility
rows.description: Within-month square root of sum of squared daily returns: $\sqrt{\sum r_t^2}$. Requires a minimum of 5 daily returns.

rows.name: Realized Signed Jump
rows.description: Within-month signed jump as the code computes it: $(\sqrt{\sum_{r>0} r_t^2} - \sqrt{\sum_{r<0} r_t^2}) / \sum_t r_t^2$, the up-minus-down volatility over the realized variance. It is not bounded by 1 and scales with one over the volatility. Requires a minimum of 5 daily returns.
rows.paper_prints: Within-month asymmetry in positive vs.\ negative squared returns: $(RV^+ - RV^-)/RV$. Requires a minimum of 5 daily returns.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row, $(RV^+ - RV^-)/RV$, reads as a ratio between -1 and 1. `stage2/lib/illiq_pandas.py` takes the square roots of the up and down sums of squares and divides their difference by the sum of squares itself, not its square root. On the 2026-09-21 panel the column runs from -2,142 to 2,254 and 90.5% of its values lie outside [-1, 1].

rows.name: Realized Skewness
rows.description: Within-month third moment of daily returns scaled by realized volatility. Requires a minimum of 5 daily returns.

rows.name: Realized Kurtosis
rows.description: Within-month fourth moment of daily returns scaled by realized volatility. Requires a minimum of 5 daily returns.

rows.name: 95% Value-at-Risk
rows.description: 5th percentile loss from the empirical distribution of monthly returns over a 36(12) rolling window.
rows.paper_prints: 5th percentile loss from empirical daily return distribution over a 36(12) rolling window.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row says daily returns. The code uses monthly ones: stage2/steps/step6_momentum.py passes lib/var_es.py the bond-month return panel, and the window is 36 months with at least 12, which is what the 36(12) in the same sentence counts.

rows.name: 90% Expected Shortfall
rows.description: Mean of worst 10% of monthly returns over a 36(12) rolling window.
rows.paper_prints: Mean of worst 10% of daily returns over a 36(12) rolling window.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row says daily returns. The code uses monthly ones: stage2/steps/step6_momentum.py passes lib/var_es.py the bond-month return panel, and the window is 36 months with at least 12, which is what the 36(12) in the same sentence counts.

rows.name: 90% Value-at-Risk
rows.description: 10th percentile loss from the empirical distribution of monthly returns over a 36(12) rolling window.
rows.paper_prints: 10th percentile loss from empirical daily return distribution over a 36(12) rolling window.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row says daily returns. The code uses monthly ones: stage2/steps/step6_momentum.py passes lib/var_es.py the bond-month return panel, and the window is 36 months with at least 12, which is what the 36(12) in the same sentence counts.

rows.name: Systematic Volatility
rows.description: Standard deviation of the systematic part of the bond's daily returns within the month, from a regression on the day's equal-weighted average return across all bonds. Requires a minimum of 5 daily returns.
rows.paper_prints: Standard deviation of systematic returns (CAPMB fitted values) within the month. Requires a minimum of 5 daily returns.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row names a CAPMB regression. The market in `stage2/lib/illiq_pandas.py` is the day's equal-weighted average daily return across every bond in the sample, not the MKTB factor.

rows.name: Idiosyncratic Volatility
rows.description: Standard deviation of the idiosyncratic part of the bond's daily returns within the month: the residual of a regression on the day's equal-weighted average return across all bonds. Requires a minimum of 5 daily returns.
rows.paper_prints: Standard deviation of idiosyncratic returns (CAPMB residuals) within the month. Requires a minimum of 5 daily returns.
rows.why_corrected: As for `dvol_sys`: the market is the day's average return across all bonds, not the MKTB factor.

rows.name: Idiosyncratic Volatility (MKT)
rows.description: Residual volatility from joint MKTRF+MKTB regression.

rows.name: Idiosyncratic Volatility (BBW)
rows.description: Residual volatility from BBW 4-factor regression.

rows.name: Idiosyncratic Volatility (VP)
rows.description: Residual volatility from VOLPSB regression.

rows.name: Idiosyncratic Skewness
rows.description: Rolling skewness of the residuals of the coskewness regression (MKTB and its square), each residual taken with that month's rolling betas. Before the bond has enough observations for the betas, its residual is the raw return.
rows.paper_prints: Skewness of residuals from coskewness regression.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row does not say how the residuals are formed. `stage2/lib/betas.py` subtracts each month's own rolling betas times the factors and fills a missing beta with 0, so the bond's first months enter the skewness window as raw returns.

rows.name: Equity Market Beta
rows.description: Beta on MKTRF from joint regression with MKTB (36-month rolling).

rows.name: Bond Market Beta
rows.description: Beta on MKTB from joint regression with MKTRF (36-month rolling).

rows.name: Bond Market Beta (Univariate)
rows.description: Beta from univariate regression on MKTB.

rows.name: Duration-Adj Market Beta
rows.description: Beta on MKTBX, from a rolling regression of the bond's return \texttt{ret\_vw} on MKTBX and TERM. The regression is on the total return; the version on the duration-adjusted return is in the \texttt{betas\_x} block.
rows.paper_prints: Beta on MKTBX from duration-adjusted CAPM.
rows.why_corrected: The printed duration-adjusted CAPM has the duration-adjusted return on the left. The panel's column comes from the `std` variant in `stage2/lib/betas.py`, which regresses `ret_vw`; the `x` variant, published in `betas_x`, regresses the duration-adjusted return.

rows.name: Term Premium Beta
rows.description: Beta on TERM, from the same regression of \texttt{ret\_vw} on MKTBX and TERM. TERM $=$ MKTB $+ r^f -$ MKTBX, the value-weighted duration-matched Treasury return, not an excess return.
rows.paper_prints: Beta on TERM $=$ MKTB $-$ MKTBX from duration-adjusted CAPM.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row defines TERM as MKTB $-$ MKTBX. `stage2/steps/step3_bbw.py` subtracts MKTBX from the raw market return, before the risk-free rate is taken off, so TERM keeps $r^f$: on the 2026-09-21 factors it equals MKTB $+ r^f -$ MKTBX to within 2e-17 in all 628 months of the merged factors. The regression is on `ret_vw`, as for `b_mktbx_dcapm`: the panel's column averages 1.05, against -0.08 in `betas_x`.

rows.name: Downside Market Beta
rows.description: Beta on $\min(\text{MKTB}, 0)$ from asymmetric market model.

rows.name: Upside Market Beta
rows.description: Beta on $\max(\text{MKTB}, 0)$ from asymmetric market model.

rows.name: Term Beta
rows.description: Beta on TERMB, from one rolling regression of the bond's return on TERMB and DEFB.
rows.paper_prints: Beta on TERMB from market regression.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row describes a market regression. As for `b_defb`: one two-factor regression on TERMB and DEFB gives both loadings.

rows.name: Daily Market Beta
rows.description: Beta from within-month daily regression on cross-sectional mean return.

rows.name: Downside Risk Beta (Univariate)
rows.description: Beta from univariate regression on DRF.

rows.name: Credit Risk Beta (Univariate)
rows.description: Beta from univariate regression on CRF.

rows.name: Liquidity Risk Beta (Univariate)
rows.description: Beta from univariate regression on LRF.

rows.name: Default Beta
rows.description: Beta on DEFB, from one rolling regression of the bond's return on TERMB and DEFB.
rows.paper_prints: Beta on DEFB from duration-adjusted market regression.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row describes a duration-adjusted market regression. Since the DEF/TERM fix, `stage2/lib/betas.py` estimates both loadings from one two-factor regression, r = a + b_term TERMB + b_def DEFB, on the bond's total return.

rows.name: VIX Innovation Beta
rows.description: Sum of contemporaneous and lagged $\Delta$VIX betas from MKTB+MKTRF regression.

rows.name: VIX Beta (Amihud)
rows.description: Sum of the betas on this month's and last month's VIX change, from a rolling regression on FF3, the VIX level, both VIX changes and the Amihud factor (AMD).
rows.paper_prints: $\Delta$VIX beta from FF3+VIX+Amihud specification.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row names one $\Delta$VIX beta. `stage2/lib/betas.py` adds the betas on the current and the lagged change (the model's `sum`), and reports the total.

rows.name: VIX Beta (PSB)
rows.description: Sum of the betas on this month's and last month's VIX change, from a rolling regression on FF3, the VIX level, both VIX changes and the Pastor-Stambaugh factor (PSB).
rows.paper_prints: $\Delta$VIX beta from FF3+VIX+PSB specification.
rows.why_corrected: As for `b_dvix_va`: `stage2/lib/betas.py` reports the sum of the betas on the current and the lagged VIX change.

rows.name: Downside VIX Beta
rows.description: Beta on $\min(\Delta\text{VIX}, 0)$ from asymmetric VIX model.

rows.name: Upside VIX Beta
rows.description: Beta on $\max(\Delta\text{VIX}, 0)$ from asymmetric VIX model.

rows.name: Pastor-Stambaugh Beta
rows.description: Beta on bond market liquidity factor PSB.

rows.name: PSB Beta (Multi-Factor)
rows.description: PSB beta controlling for FF3+MKTBX+TERM.

rows.name: Amihud Beta (Multi-Factor)
rows.description: Amihud beta controlling for FF3+MKTBX+TERM.

rows.name: Amihud Beta
rows.description: Beta on aggregate Amihud illiquidity factor.

rows.name: Coskewness Beta
rows.description: Beta on $\text{MKTB}^2$ from coskewness regression.

rows.name: VIX Level Beta
rows.description: Beta on the VIX level (divided by 100 and by $\sqrt{12}$), from a regression of the bond's daily returns within the month. Requires a minimum of 5 daily returns.
rows.paper_prints: Beta on VIX level from monthly regression.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row says a monthly regression. `stage2/lib/illiq_pandas.py` regresses the bond's daily returns on the daily VIX level within each bond-month, at least 5, as the dictionary's technical appendix already said. The VIX enters divided by 100 and by the square root of 12 (`stage2/lib/vix.py`).

rows.name: Daily VIX Innovation Beta
rows.description: Beta on the change in VIX between the bond's consecutive trade dates within the month, from a regression of its daily returns; a change across more than 5 days is left out. Requires a minimum of 5 daily returns.
rows.paper_prints: Beta on daily $\Delta$VIX within the month. Requires a minimum of 5 daily returns.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row says the daily $\Delta$VIX. `stage2/lib/illiq_pandas.py` differences VIX across the bond's own trade dates and drops a change when they are more than 5 days apart, so each change spans the same days as the return beside it.

rows.name: Illiquidity Beta
rows.description: Beta on aggregate bond market illiquidity factor.

rows.name: Macro Uncertainty Beta
rows.description: Beta on changes in Jurado, Ludvigson, and Ng (2015) macro uncertainty index.

rows.name: Real Uncertainty Beta
rows.description: Beta on changes in Jurado, Ludvigson, and Ng (2015) real uncertainty component.

rows.name: Financial Uncertainty Beta
rows.description: Beta on changes in Jurado, Ludvigson, and Ng (2015) financial uncertainty component.

rows.name: Uncertainty Level Beta
rows.description: Beta on Jurado, Ludvigson, and Ng (2015) macro uncertainty level.

rows.name: 3-Month Uncertainty Change Beta
rows.description: Beta on 3-month change in Jurado, Ludvigson, and Ng (2015) macro uncertainty.

rows.name: 6-Month Uncertainty Change Beta
rows.description: Beta on 6-month change in Jurado, Ludvigson, and Ng (2015) macro uncertainty.

rows.name: Inflation Beta
rows.description: Beta on the one-month-lagged change in the CPI level (FRED CPIAUCSL), in index points: a change in the index, not a rate of inflation.
rows.paper_prints: Beta on monthly CPI changes.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row says monthly CPI changes, which reads as inflation. `stage2/lib/factor_fetch.py` differences the CPI index lagged one month, so the factor is in index points: from -3.84 to 3.66, mean 0.451, in the 2026-09-21 factors. A point is a larger share of CPI early in the sample than now.

rows.name: Inflation Volatility Beta
rows.description: Beta on the 6-month rolling standard deviation of that lagged CPI change, in index points.
rows.paper_prints: Beta on 6-month rolling CPI volatility.
rows.why_corrected: As for `b_dcpi`: `stage2/lib/factor_fetch.py` builds the series from CPI index-point changes, not from inflation rates.

rows.name: Credit Spread Change Beta
rows.description: Beta on monthly changes in BAA-AAA spread.

rows.name: Credit Spread Level Beta
rows.description: Beta on BAA-AAA credit spread level.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row cites Dickerson, Mueller and Robotti (2023), Priced risk in corporate bonds. The credit spread level beta comes from Dickerson, Julliard and Mueller (2026), The co-pricing factor zoo, Journal of Financial Economics 182, 104295. The Stage 2 data report already cited that paper for this row.

rows.name: Intermediary Capital Beta
rows.description: Beta on the He-Kelly-Manela traded intermediary capital factor, a return less the risk-free rate, with MKTRF alongside.
rows.paper_prints: Beta on traded intermediary capital ratio.
rows.why_corrected: The printed row calls it the capital ratio. `stage2/lib/factor_fetch.py` reads HKM's `intermediary_value_weighted_investment_return`, a traded return, and the risk-free rate is subtracted when the factors are merged (`stage2/steps/compute_factors.py`).

rows.name: Realized Volatility Beta
rows.description: Beta on aggregate realized volatility factor.

rows.name: Realized Jump Beta
rows.description: Beta on aggregate realized signed jump factor.

rows.name: Level Factor Beta
rows.description: Beta on the average over key-rate U.S. Treasury yields.

rows.name: Yield Spread Beta
rows.description: Beta on yield spread factor.

rows.name: Economic Policy Uncertainty Beta
rows.description: Beta on EPU index level.

rows.name: Monetary Policy Uncertainty Beta
rows.description: Beta on monetary policy uncertainty index level.

rows.name: Tax Policy Uncertainty Beta
rows.description: Beta on the tax policy uncertainty index level (Baker-Bloom-Davis categorical EPU, column "3. Taxes"). NOT trade policy -- a separate category in the same workbook, never read.
